moat_against: Commodity assembly economics; Dell/HPE compete for the same racks
Extreme customer concentration (one customer 63% of revenue in Q2 FY2026 per press)
Total dependence on Nvidia GPU supply
Thin, falling gross margin through the strongest demand cycle in industry history
moat_for: First-mover in direct liquid cooling and rack-scale integration
Scale and early Nvidia allocation relationship
DCBBS push into higher-margin full data-center solutions
moat_justification: Speed-to-market and rack-scale/liquid-cooling integration are real but replicable; economics prove a weak moat — TTM gross margin ~10.8% (down from ~18% three years ago) against hyperscaler customers with overwhelming bargaining power, single-source Nvidia GPU dependence, and Dell/HPE selling the same capability. No proprietary silicon, software, or switching costs.
name: Super Micro Computer, Inc.
one_liner: AI rack assembler, weak 3/10 moat, whose hypergrowth consumes cash — FY2026 net income $2.23B but owner's earnings −$7.38B (working-capital build); Tier F, no hurdle-clearing price exists on filed numbers until cash conversion is proven.
